title: 10 Common Phrasal Verbs in Daily Life 👂 | Learn English with Real Examples
channel: Speak English with Bo's Slow English

lines.text: Hello everyone. Welcome to a new episode
of Bose's Slow English. In today's
video, we are going to learn 10
important phrasal verbs. A phrasal verb
is a phrase made up of one verb plus one
small word which may be a preposition or
an adverb. You may be asking why are
phrasal verbs important to know? Well,
number one, they are everywhere. Native
English speakers use phrasal verbs all
the time in their daily conversations.
Number two, it makes you sound more
natural when you use phrasal verbs in
your sentences. It helps you to sound
less formal and more fluent. And I know
the goal of studying English with me is
to become fluent eventually. Number
three, they cover daily life. From
morning routines to travel to work to
relationships, phrasal verbs describe
actions that we do every day. Number
four, they're often idiomatic. The
meaning is not always obvious from the
individual words, so they must be
learned in chunks. To summarize why you
need to pay attention to today's lesson
is when you speak English using phrasal
verbs in your sentences, it will help
you to sound more fluent and more
natural. Before we get started, please
click like, subscribe,
share with your friends, and if you
loved today's lesson, check out the
ebook below in the description. I have a
90 phrasal verb ebook available for you.
I worked very hard to put this book
together to help you to learn English.
Today I am vlogging in my office. It has
been a long time since I've vlogged in
here and I want to show you this present
that I got from Flexispot.
They sent me a chair. I needed a new
chair because I spend hours sitting down
in front of my laptop editing my videos.
So, coincidentally,
this company called Flexispot
sent me a chair. So, I would like to
thank them and I can actually teach you
several phrasal verbs using my new
chair. I am going to teach you 10
phrasal verbs. After each phrasal verb,
I will provide an example sentence. To
sit down, this means to move your body
into a sitting position. When I sit down
in this chair, I can comfortably vlog.
To hold up, this means to support
something or keep it in place. The
builtin back support holds up my lower
back to decrease tension to move around.
This means to change position or
location freely. The armrests are easy
to move around. I can turn it side to
side, up and down, backward and forward.
To pull out, this means to extend or
remove something by pulling. When I need
to rest my legs, I can pull out this
footrest
to stand up to. This means to be strong
enough to resist or last through use or
stress. The mesh feels cool against my
body. And the materials seem like
they'll stand up to daily use without
wearing out. To fit in. This means to
match well with other things in a space
or group. Even though my chair is black,
it fits in well with the rest of my
office. To turn on to make a light or
machine start working, I usually turn on
this lamp to brighten up the room. To
fluff up. This means to shake or pat
something soft so it looks bigger and
feels more comfortable. Before I sit in
this rocking chair, I fluff up the
pillow so it's more comfortable to pull
open. This means to open something by
pulling it towards you. I had to pull
open this drawer to grab a charger. To
sort out. This means to organize things
in the right order or place. I spent the
afternoon sorting out my books so that
it looks nice and organized. Let me know
in the comments which of these phrasal
verbs are new to you and also feel free
to leave your own example sentences and
I will provide corrections if it's
needed. If you loved this lesson, please
check out the 90page phrasal verb ebook
in the description below. I will see you
in the next lesson. Thank you. Bye.
